Re: Pre-service appeal of denial for cervical fusion (ACDF)  
Member: Jordan Alvarez  
Member ID: W482428991  
Reference number: POC-177B09D7A6-51151  
Requested procedure: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, CPT 22551  
Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery  

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing UnitedHealthcare’s August 11, 2026 denial of authorization for CPT 22551. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. I request reversal of the denial and authorization for the recommended C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion.

The clinical record supports a symptomatic cervical disc herniation with objective nerve-root compression and corresponding neurologic impairment:

- I have had 24 months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- My symptoms include radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- The June 4, 2026 cervical MRI shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- The MRI abnormality, distribution of symptoms, examination findings, weakness, and neurologic deficit are anatomically concordant. The imaging therefore does not represent an incidental finding; it identifies a structural lesion at the level corresponding to the clinical C6 radiculopathy.

I have also completed substantial nonoperative treatment without adequate resolution:

- Supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, for eight weeks from May 14, 2026 through July 9, 2026, with 18 visits completed. The physical therapy discharge note documents this course.
- NSAID treatment for four months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 3, 2026, which produced only four weeks of partial relief.

The requested surgery is being recommended after prolonged symptoms, failure of supervised conservative treatment, persistent radicular pain and numbness, weakness, and objective neurologic findings that correspond to the MRI-confirmed C5-C6 disc herniation and C6 nerve-root compression.

The publicly posted UnitedHealthcare commercial policy is titled Spinal Fusion and Decompression – UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy, policy number 2026T0639I, effective April 1, 2026. It states: “Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances.” It also states: “For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Decompression +/- Fusion, Cervical.”

I have not been provided the detailed InterQual cervical criteria or the specific criterion that UnitedHealthcare determined was not met. Please identify in the appeal decision the exact cervical InterQual criteria, version and date used, the particular requirement allegedly not satisfied, and the clinical evidence relied upon. Please also provide the complete clinical rationale for concluding that the June 4, 2026 MRI does not support the requested procedure.

For completeness, the record does not identify active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. BMI is 29. These factors do not explain the persistent neurologic symptoms or the C5-C6 MRI findings.

Please conduct a full and fair reconsideration of this pre-service denial. Based on the concordance between the MRI, symptoms, examination, weakness, and neurologic deficit, together with the documented failure of conservative treatment, I request authorization for CPT 22551 at C5-C6.

Please notify me and Dr. Lindqvist in writing of the appeal determination. If UnitedHealthcare maintains the denial, please provide the specific medical-necessity criteria applied, the exact reason each criterion was considered unmet, and instructions for any further appeal or external review.

Sincerely,

Jordan Alvarez
